solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: On vacation, repeatedly exasperating guests before noon order such dish

indicators.note: a vacated word is emptied of its middle, and this happens to each of the three words in turn, leaving only their outside letters

parts.note: an edict is an official order or decree

explanation.surface: Someone irritably ordering a brunch dish for guests before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation, repeatedly' empties each of three words in turn, not just one. 'such dish' leans on the scene for its definition: the dish ordered before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict is a classic brunch dish of poached eggs and hollandaise on a muffin, typically eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Eyes on Amy wrongly getting reward for little effort

indicators.note: letters set down wrongly are put in the wrong order, so these words must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing up Amy and wrongly being rewarded without trying.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy money is cash gained without hard work, so it is a payoff for minimal exertion.

clue.text: He and CO seen together, symbolic of what?

definitions.text: He and CO seen together, symbolic of what?

parts.words: He and CO seen together, symbolic of what?
parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium and CO the formula for carbon monoxide; both stand for substances of the same physical state

explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man and 'CO' a company or commanding officer; read as chemistry, they are helium and carbon monoxide.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium and carbon monoxide are both vapours at room temperature, so what they symbolise together is this category of substance.

clue.text: Pouch aboard airline guards regularly ignored

indicators.note: being aboard something means being inside it, so these letters go within the airline's letters

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is ignored, keeping the even-numbered ones

explanation.surface: Something about a pouch carried on a plane being skipped by security staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' drops the odd letters of guards (G, A, D), leaving URS to go aboard BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bursa is an anatomical sac or fluid-filled bag, for instance cushioning a joint.

clue.text: Silent first officer, inept to forget uniform

parts.note: No. 1 (Number One) is naval slang for the first lieutenant, written NO plus the numeral 1 as I

indicators.note: forgetting something leaves it out, so a letter is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: useless means inept or incompetent
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A senior officer stays quiet, too incompetent to remember his uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number One' is the Royal Navy's informal name for a ship's first lieutenant, written No. 1, with the 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noiseless makes no sound at all, so it is silent.

clue.text: Show contempt for dad overturning fruit split

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for showing them disrespect

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturning a word turns it upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A child disdains a father who knocks over the fruit bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' looks like a description of the fruit, but it is the slang verb meaning to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is slang for leaving abruptly, which is to vanish from a scene.

clue.text: Split, Croatia's top port?

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: Asking whether Split is Croatia's leading harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as the Croatian port city, but it is the definition, and 'port' is the nautical word for left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a fissure or division, so as an adjective it means divided in two.

clue.text: Intended new model will break virtually all rules

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so these letters split the other word
virtually all means nearly all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a code is a set of rules
a template is a model or pattern to copy

explanation.surface: A new design is meant to flout almost every regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually all' drops the last letter of the rules word, and 'will break' sets the new model inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemplated, as in a planned move, means considered or intended as a course of action.

clue.text: Place of retreat when becoming overwhelmed by Love Island?

indicators.note: something overwhelmed by another is engulfed by it, so this word goes inside the others

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written O
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A retreat on the reality show Love Island, where contestants get swamped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love Island' reads as the TV show but splits into love (O) and Island (IS).
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is figuratively a peaceful refuge or haven amid surrounding turmoil.

clue.text: Net prices fixed for review once again

indicators.note: something fixed has been rearranged or doctored, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Prices that have been rigged are up for another review.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinspect is to examine or check a second time.

clue.text: Amusing trait strangely causing great distress

indicators.note: letters arranged strangely are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A funny quirk that oddly upsets people.
explanation.definitionFit: Traumatising something or someone inflicts deep emotional shock and lasting upset.

clue.text: 'Estimated period to complete work is surprisingly elastic', this writer interjects

indicators.note: to interject is to throw something in between, so these letters go inside the others
letters behaving surprisingly end up in an unexpected order

parts.note: this writer is the setter, meaning me

explanation.surface: The setter butts in to say a project deadline is surprisingly flexible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges elastic into TISCALE, and 'interjects' puts ME after its first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A timescale is the length of time over which a job is planned to happen.

clue.text: Bread for variety of birds

definitions.meaning: a family of brightly coloured tropical birds

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flatbread and a group of colourful Old World songbirds.

clue.text: Obstinate type describes elected American congressman originally as very unimportant

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw around, as when a circle is described, so the first word goes round the others

parts.note: a mule is a byword for stubbornness
a winning candidate is in

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A stubborn politician dismisses an elected American congressman as unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuscule means extremely small, hence trivial or of no significance.

clue.text: Spend lots of money installing switch in jet

indicators.note: installing something puts it inside, so the jet's letters go around the switch's

parts.note: a spout is a jet of liquid
a switch is a thin whip, and to lash is to whip

explanation.surface: Someone flying by jet having a new switch fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' and 'jet' both look like hardware, but a switch is a whip (LASH) and a jet is a spurt (SPOUT).
explanation.definitionFit: To splash out is a British idiom for spending freely or extravagantly.

clue.text: Experienced university oarsman's back on river

indicators.note: the back of the rower's word is its final letter

parts.note: the Derwent is a river, in fact several in England

explanation.surface: A college rower's back problem on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the rower's letters above the river. The Derwent is one of several English rivers of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwent is the past tense of undergo, meaning went through or experienced.

clue.text: Record second case of occultism in Derby home

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Recording a second occult case at a house in Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' looks like the English city, but it is the horse race run at Epsom Downs in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby, Britain's famous flat horse race, is run each year at this racecourse town.

clue.text: Shabby state of children in over half of Essex

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants

indicators.note: over half of a five-letter word is more than half its letters, here the first three

explanation.surface: Children in most of the county live in a run-down condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county north-east of London; 'over half of' takes its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Seediness is a sordid, run-down or disreputable condition, so it is a shabby state.

clue.text: Faithful ally, excited to receive Oscar

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so this letter goes inside
excited letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A devoted friend thrilled to win an Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal means steadfast in allegiance, as is a faithful supporter.

clue.text: Turn away from East London footballers, shortly after endless team reverses

indicators.note: after places the footballers' name after the reversed team
a word that reverses is read backwards
endless means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a side is a team
Leyton Orient, an East London football club, is often called simply Orient

explanation.surface: East London football fans turn their back on a team going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims SIDE to SID and 'reverses' turns it to DIS. Leyton Orient is a football club based in East London.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient originally meant to face the east, so to disorient is literally to turn from that direction.

clue.text: Errors when texting certain blood donors, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: type Os are donors with blood group O, the universal donors

explanation.surface: Mistakes made in texts by blood donors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type O's', people with blood group O, said aloud match the word for slips on the keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing mistake, common when tapping out messages on a phone.

clue.text: Reportedly took steps to apply adhesive

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is told by word of mouth, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: paced means walked with measured steps

explanation.surface: Someone said to have taken measures to glue something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took steps' looks like 'took measures', but it means walked.
explanation.definitionFit: To paste is to stick something down using glue, as wallpaper is pasted.

clue.text: Regulations initially one changes, covering fifty competitions

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: covering means surrounding, so the fifty goes inside the changes

parts.note: varies means changes
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Rules on how one changes, covering about fifty contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivalries are contests or ongoing competitive struggles between parties.

clue.text: Retired relatives keeping energetic

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going backwards, so the letters read in reverse
keeping means holding within, so the letters sit inside the word

explanation.surface: Pensioned-off family members keeping full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' holds LATIV inside relatives, and 'Retired' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital can mean lively and full of vigour, as in a vital performance.

clue.text: Yarn, story about vacuous showgirl

indicators.note: about means around, so the story wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A tall tale about an airheaded showgirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a tale to go with story, but it is the thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread used for stockings and gloves.

clue.text: Untrustworthy daughter, she is not reforming

indicators.note: reforming the letters means shaping them into a new order

explanation.surface: A daughter who cannot be trusted because she is not changing her ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dishonest lies or cheats, so cannot be relied upon.

clue.text: Tail end of film we skipped

indicators.note: skipped means left out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a western is a film genre

explanation.surface: We missed the end of the movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear of a ship, hence the back part of anything.

clue.text: Having lost weight, injured otters eat well; do they always avoid slugs?

indicators.note: injured letters are damaged and come out jumbled
having lost something means dropping it, so the letter goes from the word

explanation.surface: Slimmed-down hurt otters eat well, and asks whether they shun slugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slugs' looks like garden pests the otters might eat, but means slugs of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Teetotallers abstain from alcohol, so they never knock back a slug, a quick gulp of spirits.
